# SB-1046 Safety bulletin: noise exposure
Revision: Rev B
Plant: P1, line P1-L4
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01

Hazard description
This bulletin addresses elevated noise exposure at the Heat Treat CNC turning center and adjacent work zones on line P1-L4. Prolonged or repeated exposure to elevated noise levels can cause permanent hearing loss, communication failures during critical operations, and increased risk of incident due to missed warnings. Typical contributors in the subject area include machine cutting and clamping cycles, exhaust and ventilation flow paths, and tool change impacts. Noise may also be amplified by nearby sheet metal surfaces and enclosures that reflect sound into operator positions and maintenance access points.

Background and rationale
A recent review of operator reports and maintenance observations identified the Heat Treat CNC turning center as a primary source requiring targeted controls. Engineering assessment indicated that a combination of machine maintenance, localized attenuation, and administrative practices will reduce employee exposure without reducing productivity. Maintaining lubrication and mechanical condition has a direct influence on bearing and gear noise; lubrication regimen consistency reduces intermittent high-frequency peaks that occur when components are under load. The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours. Compliance with this interval is a foundational control for noise reduction and for ensuring predictable acoustic behaviour during production cycles.

Affected equipment
- EQ-P1-L4-CN01 — Heat Treat CNC turning center #1, primary focus of this bulletin.
- Adjacent fixed workstations and access aisles on P1-L4 that share the acoustic envelope with EQ-P1-L4-CN01.
- Portable equipment routinely operated within the line P1-L4 area during machining cycles.

Required controls
Engineering controls
- Ensure way lube refill interval adherence as stated: The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours. Document each refill in the machine maintenance log.
- Inspect and secure loose panels or covers that may resonate during operation. Replace or re-seat fasteners and gaskets using shop-standard parts and methods referenced in MM-P1-L4-CN01.
- Install or verify integrity of available acoustic enclosures and sound-damping materials on machine housings. Where retrofit attenuation is applied, confirm that ventilation and access remain compliant with SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-05.
Administrative controls
- Schedule way lube refills and related checks to align with production changeovers to minimize disruption and ensure consistent application. Record the date, time, and technician ID in the maintenance log accompanying MM-P1-L4-CN01.
- Limit nonessential personnel in the immediate acoustic zone during noisy operations. Use signage and access control procedures consistent with SOP-P1-L4-02.
- Rotate assignment of personnel with potential exposure to reduce individual accumulated exposure, following line scheduling practices. Ensure affected employees receive the required training and hearing conservation materials referenced in SOP-P1-L4-05.
Personal protective equipment
- Provide and mandate hearing protection for operators and maintenance personnel entering the defined exposure zone. Selection and fit-testing should be documented in accordance with SOP-P1-L4-05.
- Require supervisors to verify PPE use during operations and to record compliance observations in the site safety log.

Implementation steps and examples
- Maintenance example: On machine cooldown or scheduled access, perform way lube refill as specified and log completion. A typical entry should include machine ID EQ-P1-L4-CN01, maintenance action "way lube refill", the phrase "40 hours" where required by the log template, technician initials, and any observations of abnormal noise sources.
- Work practice example: When an operator changes tooling, ensure panels are closed and vibration-isolating mounts are engaged before resuming cutting. If an operator reports an intermittent squeal, tag the machine out of service and notify maintenance per MM-P1-L4-CN01 procedures until the source is remedied.
- Acoustic verification example: After implementation of new damping material, perform a listening test and document operator feedback per SOP-P1-L4-05. If persistent discrete tones are reported, create a maintenance action per MM-P1-L4-CN01 and schedule follow-up.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entries for way lube refill of EQ-P1-L4-CN01, including the explicit refill interval reference: The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours.
- Inspection reports for covers, fasteners, and acoustic materials. Reference MM-P1-L4-CN01 for the preferred inspection checklist.
- Training, PPE issuance, and fit-testing records maintained per SOP-P1-L4-05.
- Access control and exposure-zone signage placement records, and any incident reports or employee complaints logged per SOP-P1-L4-02.

Monitoring and follow-up
- Supervisors on P1-L4 will review maintenance logs weekly and escalate any missed way lube refill entries or recurrent noise complaints to maintenance leadership and safety. All corrective actions should reference MM-P1-L4-CN01 for repair procedures and SOP-P1-L4-05 for employee communications.
- Any modification to machine enclosures or ventilation must be accompanied by a risk assessment and re-evaluation of noise controls, with documentation retained alongside the machine file.

Effective date
This bulletin is effective immediately upon issuance. All required controls must be implemented and initial records submitted to the P1-L4 safety coordinator. Refer to MM-P1-L4-CN01, SOP-P1-L4-02, and SOP-P1-L4-05 for related procedures and forms.
